options.C: A tax that takes a higher proportion of income from lower-income taxpayers
options.D: A tax that is imposed only on the rich

questions.explanation: A progressive tax takes a higher proportion of income as income rises.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is proportional taxation?

options.A: A tax that takes a higher proportion of income as income rises
options.B: A tax that applies the same tax rate to the relevant tax base regardless of its size
options.C: A tax that takes a higher proportion of income from lower-income taxpayers
options.D: A tax that is imposed only on luxury goods

questions.explanation: A proportional tax applies the same tax rate to the relevant tax base regardless of its size.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is regressive taxation?

options.A: A tax that takes a higher proportion of income as income rises
options.B: A tax that applies the same rate to all taxpayers
options.C: A tax that takes a higher proportion of income from lower-income taxpayers than from higher-income taxpayers
options.D: A tax that is imposed only on the poor

questions.explanation: A regressive tax takes a higher proportion of income from lower-income taxpayers than from higher-income taxpayers.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is tax incidence?

options.A: The person legally required to pay the tax
options.B: Who ultimately bears the economic burden of a tax, which may differ from the person legally required to pay it
options.C: The rate at which a tax is levied
options.D: The total revenue collected from a tax

questions.explanation: Tax incidence refers to who ultimately bears the economic burden of a tax, which may differ from the person legally required to pay it.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is tax evasion?

options.A: The use of legal arrangements to reduce tax liability
options.B: The illegal non-payment or underpayment of tax through concealment, false reporting or other unlawful means
options.C: The shifting of the tax burden to another person
options.D: The payment of taxes on time

questions.explanation: Tax evasion is the illegal non-payment or underpayment of tax through concealment, false reporting or other unlawful means.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is tax avoidance?

options.A: The illegal non-payment of tax
options.B: The use of legal arrangements to reduce tax liability, though abusive arrangements may be challenged under anti-avoidance rules
options.C: The shifting of the tax burden to another person
options.D: The evasion of customs duties

questions.explanation: Tax avoidance is the use of legal arrangements to reduce tax liability, though abusive arrangements may be challenged under anti-avoidance rules.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is Goods and Services Tax (GST)?

options.A: A destination-based, value-added indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, with input tax credit subject to statutory rules
options.B: A direct tax on income
options.C: A tax on imports only
options.D: A tax on agricultural produce only

questions.explanation: GST is a destination-based, value-added indirect tax on the supply of goods and services, with input tax credit subject to statutory rules.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: When was GST introduced in India?

options.A: 1 April 2016
options.B: 1 July 2017
options.C: 1 January 2018
options.D: 15 August 2017

questions.explanation: GST was introduced on 1 July 2017.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What are CGST and SGST?

options.A: CGST is Central GST and SGST is State GST, generally levied together on an intra-State taxable supply
options.B: CGST is Central GST and SGST is State GST, generally levied on inter-State supplies
options.C: CGST is Integrated GST and SGST is State GST
options.D: CGST is Customs GST and SGST is Service GST

questions.explanation: CGST is Central GST and SGST is State GST, generally levied together on an intra-State taxable supply.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is IGST?

options.A: Integrated GST, generally levied on intra-State supplies
options.B: Integrated GST, generally levied on inter-State supplies and imports under the GST framework
options.C: Income GST, levied on income
options.D: International GST, levied on exports

questions.explanation: Integrated GST (IGST) is generally levied on inter-State supplies and imports under the GST framework.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the GST Council?

options.A: A constitutional body under Article 279A that recommends GST rates, exemptions, model laws and other matters
options.B: A statutory body under the RBI Act
options.C: A body that prepares the Union Budget
options.D: A body that regulates the stock market

questions.explanation: The GST Council is a constitutional body under Article 279A that recommends GST rates, exemptions, model laws and other matters.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is non-tax revenue?

options.A: Government revenue from taxes only
options.B: Government revenue from sources other than taxes, such as fees, fines, dividends, interest receipts and service charges
options.C: Government borrowing
options.D: Government expenditure

questions.explanation: Non-tax revenue is government revenue from sources other than taxes, such as fees, fines, dividends, interest receipts and service charges.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is public expenditure?

options.A: Spending by government on administration, defence, infrastructure, welfare, education, health and other public purposes
options.B: Income received by government from taxes
options.C: Borrowing by government
options.D: Debt owed by government

questions.explanation: Public expenditure is spending by government on administration, defence, infrastructure, welfare, education, health and other public purposes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is revenue expenditure?

options.A: Expenditure that generally creates assets or reduces liabilities
options.B: Expenditure that generally does not create assets or directly reduce liabilities, such as salaries, subsidies, pensions and interest payments
options.C: Expenditure on infrastructure only
options.D: Expenditure on repayment of loans

questions.explanation: Revenue expenditure is expenditure that generally does not create assets or directly reduce liabilities, such as salaries, subsidies, pensions and interest payments.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is capital expenditure?

options.A: Expenditure that generally does not create assets or reduce liabilities
options.B: Expenditure generally creates assets or reduces liabilities, such as spending on infrastructure or repayment of certain loans
options.C: Expenditure on salaries and pensions
options.D: Expenditure on subsidies

questions.explanation: Capital expenditure generally creates assets or reduces liabilities, such as spending on infrastructure or repayment of certain loans.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is public debt?

options.A: The outstanding borrowing liability of government
options.B: The total tax revenue of government
options.C: The total expenditure of government
options.D: The total assets of government

questions.explanation: Public debt is the outstanding borrowing liability of government.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is internal debt?

options.A: Government borrowing from sources within the country
options.B: Government borrowing from foreign sources
options.C: Government borrowing from international organisations
options.D: Government borrowing from non-residents

questions.explanation: Internal debt is government borrowing from sources within the country.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is external debt?

options.A: Government borrowing from sources within the country
options.B: Borrowing from non-resident or foreign sources, according to the relevant statistical definition
options.C: Government borrowing from the central bank
options.D: Government borrowing from commercial banks

questions.explanation: External debt is borrowing from non-resident or foreign sources, according to the relevant statistical definition.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is fiscal policy?

options.A: The use of government taxation, expenditure and borrowing to influence economic activity, resource allocation and income distribution
options.B: The use of interest rates and money supply to influence the economy
options.C: The regulation of the stock market
options.D: The management of foreign exchange reserves

questions.explanation: Fiscal policy is the use of government taxation, expenditure and borrowing to influence economic activity, resource allocation and income distribution.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is a government budget?

options.A: An annual financial statement of estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year, presented under constitutional and statutory procedures
options.B: A statement of a company's profits and losses
options.C: A statement of household income and expenditure
options.D: A statement of the central bank's monetary policy

questions.explanation: A government budget is an annual financial statement of estimated receipts and expenditure for a financial year, presented under constitutional and statutory procedures.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which article provides for the Annual Financial Statement of the Union Government?

options.A: Article 110
options.B: Article 112
options.C: Article 266
options.D: Article 280

questions.explanation: Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement of the Union Government.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Who presents the Union Budget in Parliament?

options.A: The President of India
options.B: The Prime Minister of India
options.C: The Union Finance Minister presents the Union Budget on behalf of the Government
options.D: The RBI Governor

questions.explanation: The Union Finance Minister presents the Union Budget on behalf of the Government.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is a revenue deficit?

options.A: The excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding debt-creating capital receipts
options.B: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts
options.C: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments
options.D: Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets

questions.explanation: Revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is a fiscal deficit?

options.A: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts
options.B: The excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding debt-creating capital receipts, under the standard Indian budget definition
options.C: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments
options.D: Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets

questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit is the excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding debt-creating capital receipts, under the standard Indian budget definition.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is a primary deficit?

options.A: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts
options.B: The excess of total expenditure over total receipts excluding debt-creating capital receipts
options.C: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments
options.D: Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets

questions.explanation: Primary deficit is fiscal deficit minus interest payments.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is an effective revenue deficit?

options.A: Revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets, under the Indian budget framework
options.B: The excess of total expenditure over total receipts
options.C: Fiscal deficit minus interest payments
options.D: The excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts

questions.explanation: Effective revenue deficit is revenue deficit minus grants for creation of capital assets, under the Indian budget framework.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the formula for fiscal deficit?

options.A: Fiscal deficit = Revenue expenditure - Revenue receipts
options.B: Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts)
options.C: Fiscal deficit = Fiscal deficit - Interest payments
options.D: Fiscal deficit = Revenue deficit - Grants for creation of capital assets

questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit = Total expenditure - (Revenue receipts + Non-debt capital receipts).

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the formula for revenue deficit?

options.A: Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure - Revenue receipts
options.B: Revenue deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts
options.C: Revenue deficit = Fiscal deficit - Interest payments
options.D: Revenue deficit = Fiscal deficit + Interest payments

questions.explanation: Revenue deficit = Revenue expenditure - Revenue receipts.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the formula for primary deficit?

options.A: Primary deficit = Total expenditure - Total receipts
options.B: Primary deficit = Revenue expenditure - Revenue receipts
options.C: Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit - Interest payments
options.D: Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit + Interest payments

questions.explanation: Primary deficit = Fiscal deficit - Interest payments.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is deficit financing?

options.A: Financing a budget surplus through government savings
options.B: Financing a budget deficit through borrowing, monetary financing or other deficit-financing methods, depending on the context
options.C: Financing government expenditure through taxes only
options.D: Financing government expenditure through foreign aid only

questions.explanation: Deficit financing refers to financing a budget deficit through borrowing, monetary financing or other deficit-financing methods, depending on the context.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the FRBM Act?

options.A: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 establishes a framework for fiscal discipline and transparency at the Union level, with targets and rules subject to amendments and policy changes
options.B: The Financial Regulation and Banking Management Act, 2003
options.C: The Foreign Exchange Regulation and Business Management Act, 2003
options.D: The Federal Reserve and Budget Management Act, 2003

questions.explanation: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2003 establishes a framework for fiscal discipline and transparency at the Union level, with targets and rules subject to amendments and policy changes.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is a subsidy?

options.A: A compulsory payment to the government
options.B: Financial assistance or a price-support measure provided by government to reduce costs or encourage specified activities
options.C: A tax on goods and services
options.D: A loan provided by the government

questions.explanation: A subsidy is financial assistance or a price-support measure provided by government to reduce costs or encourage specified activities.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is disinvestment?

options.A: The sale by government of part or all of its ownership stake in a public sector enterprise
options.B: The purchase of private companies by the government
options.C: The transfer of ownership from the private sector to the public sector
options.D: The reduction of government expenditure

questions.explanation: Disinvestment is the sale by government of part or all of its ownership stake in a public sector enterprise.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is privatisation?

options.A: The sale of government equity in a public sector enterprise
options.B: The transfer of ownership or control of an enterprise or activity from the public sector to private ownership or management
options.C: The nationalisation of private enterprises
options.D: The reduction of government expenditure

questions.explanation: Privatisation is the transfer of ownership or control of an enterprise or activity from the public sector to private ownership or management.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the difference between disinvestment and privatisation?

options.A: Disinvestment means selling government equity; it becomes privatisation when the sale results in transfer of management control or ownership to private hands
options.B: Disinvestment means transferring management control; privatisation means selling government equity
options.C: Disinvestment and privatisation are the same thing
options.D: Disinvestment is the purchase of private companies; privatisation is the sale of government companies

questions.explanation: Disinvestment means selling government equity; it becomes privatisation when the sale results in transfer of management control or ownership to private hands.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the Finance Commission's role in public finance?

options.A: It recommends tax devolution between the Union and States and principles for grants-in-aid under Article 280
options.B: It formulates the Union Budget
options.C: It determines the repo rate
options.D: It regulates the stock market

questions.explanation: The Finance Commission recommends tax devolution between the Union and States and principles for grants-in-aid under Article 280.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the Consolidated Fund of India?

options.A: The fund under Article 266 that receives government revenues, loans raised and loan recoveries; withdrawals require appropriation in accordance with the Constitution
options.B: The fund under Article 267 used for urgent unforeseen expenditure
options.C: The fund under Article 266 that includes money held by government in a fiduciary or banking capacity
options.D: The fund under Article 280 that recommends tax devolution

questions.explanation: The Consolidated Fund of India under Article 266 receives government revenues, loans raised and loan recoveries; withdrawals require appropriation in accordance with the Constitution.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the Contingency Fund of India?

options.A: The fund under Article 266 that receives government revenues
options.B: The fund under Article 267 that is an imprest fund used for urgent unforeseen expenditure, subject to later legislative authorisation
options.C: The fund under Article 266 that includes money held by government in a fiduciary capacity
options.D: The fund under Article 280 that recommends tax devolution

questions.explanation: The Contingency Fund of India under Article 267 is an imprest fund used for urgent unforeseen expenditure, subject to later legislative authorisation.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the Public Account of India?

options.A: The fund under Article 266 that receives government revenues and loans
options.B: The fund under Article 267 used for urgent unforeseen expenditure
options.C: The fund under Article 266 that includes money held by government in a fiduciary or banking capacity, such as provident fund and small savings receipts
options.D: The fund under Article 280 that recommends tax devolution

questions.explanation: The Public Account under Article 266 includes money held by government in a fiduciary or banking capacity, such as provident fund and small savings receipts.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the difference between the Consolidated Fund and Public Account?

options.A: The Consolidated Fund contains government revenues and borrowings and is subject to appropriation; the Public Account contains funds held by government in trust or as a banker, with different withdrawal rules
options.B: The Consolidated Fund contains funds held in trust; the Public Account contains government revenues
options.C: Both funds have the same withdrawal rules
options.D: The Consolidated Fund is used for urgent unforeseen expenditure; the Public Account is subject to appropriation

questions.explanation: The Consolidated Fund contains government revenues and borrowings and is subject to appropriation; the Public Account contains funds held by government in trust or as a banker, with different withdrawal rules.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is economic development?

options.A: A broad process of improving living standards, capabilities, productivity, opportunities and the structure of an economy
options.B: An increase in real output or income only
options.C: An increase in the general price level
options.D: An increase in the money supply

questions.explanation: Economic development is a broad process of improving living standards, capabilities, productivity, opportunities and the structure of an economy.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the difference between economic growth and development?

options.A: Economic growth measures an increase in real output or income; economic development includes broader changes in health, education, equality, institutions and quality of life
options.B: Economic growth is broader than economic development
options.C: Economic growth and development are the same thing
options.D: Economic development measures only an increase in real output

questions.explanation: Economic growth measures an increase in real output or income; economic development includes broader changes in health, education, equality, institutions and quality of life.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is human development?

options.A: The expansion of people's capabilities and choices so that they can lead long, healthy, knowledgeable and decent lives
options.B: An increase in real output or income
options.C: An increase in the general price level
options.D: An increase in the money supply

questions.explanation: Human development is the expansion of people's capabilities and choices so that they can lead long, healthy, knowledgeable and decent lives.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Who developed the human development approach associated with the Human Development Report?

options.A: Amartya Sen
options.B: Mahbub ul Haq, drawing on Amartya Sen's capability approach
options.C: Adam Smith
options.D: John Maynard Keynes

questions.explanation: The human development approach associated with the Human Development Report is strongly associated with Mahbub ul Haq, drawing on Amartya Sen's capability approach.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What is the Human Development Index (HDI)?

options.A: A composite measure of average achievement in health, education and standard of living
options.B: A measure of income inequality
options.C: A measure of unemployment
options.D: A measure of inflation

questions.explanation: HDI is a composite measure of average achievement in health, education and standard of living.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: Which organisation publishes the Human Development Report and HDI?

options.A: World Bank
options.B: United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
options.C: International Monetary Fund
options.D: World Trade Organization

questions.explanation: The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) publishes the Human Development Report and HDI.

questions.subject: Economics
questions.question: What are the three dimensions of HDI?
